blocks.html: Channel Sales is a sales strategy in which a company sells its products or services through third-party partners—such as distributors, resellers, agents, or value-added resellers (VARs)—instead of selling directly to end customers.

Channel sales enables businesses to expand their market reach by leveraging external partners who already have established networks, customer relationships, and regional expertise. This approach is especially valuable for scaling into new markets without building a large in-house sales force.
In a channel sales model, companies collaborate with partners who promote, sell, and sometimes support their products or services. Key components include:

items.html: Providing training, tools, and sales enablement resources
Offering incentives such as margins, commissions, or rebates
Supporting partners with marketing and co-selling initiatives

blocks.html: Expands market reach and geographic presence
Partners act as an extension of the company’s sales team, helping drive revenue and customer acquisition.

A software company partners with regional resellers who bundle its solution with their own services and sell it to local businesses, allowing the company to penetrate new markets without direct sales efforts.

Channel sales is a powerful strategy for scaling business growth through partnerships. By empowering third-party partners, companies can access new customers, markets, and revenue opportunities more efficiently.
